```{r setup-chunk, include=FALSE}
# load libraries
library(shinyjs)
library(htmltools)
library(knitr)
library(flexdashboard)
library(lubridate)
library(bslib)
library(shiny)
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(plotly)
library(MASS)
library(R0)
library(DT)
library(EpiEstim)
library(incidence2)
library(visNetwork)
library(webshot)
library(webshot2)
library(officer)
library(networkD3)
library(highcharter)
library(fitdistrplus)
library(stringr)
library(rstan)
library(loo)

# suppress browser redirect on Stan warnings
options(warn = -1) 
rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)

# the mcmc sampler starts from this seed, so the same data and settings give the
# same estimates on every run. change it to check that a result does not depend
# on the seed.
STAN_SEED <- 20260423

# date parsing function
parse_date <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(as.character(x))
  parsed <- lubridate::parse_date_time(x, orders = c("dmy", "ymd", "mdy"), quiet = TRUE)
  as.Date(parsed)
}

# --- input checks ----------------------------------------------------------
# rows the app cannot use were previously dropped without a word, so a typo in a
# date or a transmission link that points at no one looked exactly like clean
# data. every page now marks each row with what became of it, shows the panel
# below above its preview, and previews the parsed values rather than the raw
# text of the file.

# values that were supplied but could not be read as a date
unreadable_values <- function(raw, parsed) {
  raw <- trimws(as.character(raw))
  blank <- !nzchar(raw) | is.na(raw) | toupper(raw) %in% c("NA", "N/A", "NULL", "-")
  unique(raw[!blank & is.na(parsed)])
}

# turns a status column into one readable line per problem, with examples
problems_from_status <- function(status, examples = list()) {
  bad <- status[status != "used"]
  if (!length(bad)) return(list())
  tab <- sort(table(bad), decreasing = TRUE)
  lapply(names(tab), function(k) {
    n <- as.integer(tab[[k]])
    txt <- sprintf("%d row%s: %s", n, if (n == 1) "" else "s", sub("^excluded: ", "", k))
    ex <- examples[[k]]
    if (!is.null(ex) && length(ex)) {
      txt <- paste0(txt, " (for example: ",
                    paste0("\u201c", utils::head(ex, 3), "\u201d", collapse = ", "), ")")
    }
    txt
  })
}

# the panel shown above each dataset preview
data_check_panel <- function(n_read, n_used, problems = list(),
                             used_label = "used in the analysis",
                             out_label  = "left out") {
  n_out <- n_read - n_used
  good  <- n_out == 0 && !length(problems)
  htmltools::div(
    style = paste0(
      "border-left:4px solid ", if (good) "#2E7D32" else "#B26A00", ";",
      "background:", if (good) "#EDF7ED" else "#FFF4E5", ";",
      "padding:10px 14px;margin:6px 0 12px 0;border-radius:4px;",
      "font-size:14px;line-height:1.5;color:#222222;"
    ),
    htmltools::tags$b(sprintf(
      "%d row%s in the current selection, %d %s, %d %s.",
      n_read, if (n_read == 1) "" else "s", n_used, used_label, n_out, out_label)),
    if (length(problems)) {
      htmltools::tags$ul(style = "margin:6px 0 0 0;padding-left:18px;",
                         lapply(problems, htmltools::tags$li))
    } else {
      htmltools::div(style = "margin-top:2px;", "Every row could be read.")
    },
    htmltools::div(
      style = "margin-top:6px;font-size:13px;color:#555555;",
      "The table below shows the values as the app read them. The status column says what happened to each row."
    )
  )
}

# helper functions for model fitting (MLE pages)
fit_parametric_model <- function(data, dist, shift_val = 0) {
  data_fit <- data + shift_val
  
  fit <- tryCatch({
    MASS::fitdistr(data_fit, dist)
  }, error = function(e) return(NULL))
  
  if(is.null(fit)) return(NULL)
  
  est <- fit$estimate
  
  if (dist == "lognormal") {
    mean_val <- exp(est["meanlog"] + est["sdlog"]^2 / 2)
    var_val <- (exp(est["sdlog"]^2) - 1) * exp(2 * est["meanlog"] + est["sdlog"]^2)
    sd_val <- sqrt(var_val)
    ci_95 <- qlnorm(0.95, est["meanlog"], est["sdlog"])
    
    raw_params <- data.frame(
      parameter = c("estimate.meanlog", "estimate.sdlog", "sd.meanlog", "sd.sdlog"),
      value = round(c(est["meanlog"], est["sdlog"], fit$sd["meanlog"], fit$sd["sdlog"]), 2)
    )
    
  } else if (dist == "weibull") {
    mean_val <- est["scale"] * gamma(1 + 1/est["shape"])
    var_val <- est["scale"]^2 * (gamma(1 + 2/est["shape"]) - (gamma(1 + 1/est["shape"]))^2)
    sd_val <- sqrt(var_val)
    ci_95 <- qweibull(0.95, est["shape"], est["scale"])
    
    raw_params <- data.frame(
      parameter = c("estimate.shape", "estimate.scale", "sd.shape", "sd.scale"),
      value = round(c(est["shape"], est["scale"], fit$sd["shape"], fit$sd["scale"]), 2)
    )
    
  } else if (dist == "gamma") {
    mean_val <- est["shape"] / est["rate"]
    var_val <- est["shape"] / (est["rate"]^2)
    sd_val <- sqrt(var_val)
    ci_95 <- qgamma(0.95, est["shape"], est["rate"])
    
    raw_params <- data.frame(
      parameter = c("estimate.shape", "estimate.rate", "sd.shape", "sd.rate"),
      value = round(c(est["shape"], est["rate"], fit$sd["shape"], fit$sd["rate"]), 2)
    )
    
  } else if (dist == "normal") {
    mean_val <- est["mean"]
    sd_val <- est["sd"]
    ci_95 <- qnorm(0.95, mean_val, sd_val)
    var_val <- sd_val^2
    
    raw_params <- data.frame(
      parameter = c("estimate.mean", "estimate.sd", "sd.mean", "sd.sd"),
      value = round(c(est["mean"], est["sd"], fit$sd["mean"], fit$sd["sd"]), 2)
    )
  }
  
  # a skewed distribution fitted to data moved to the right is a shifted
  # distribution: report the shift next to its parameters, and put the moments
  # back on to the observed scale
  if (shift_val != 0) {
    raw_params <- rbind(raw_params,
                        data.frame(parameter = "shift.applied",
                                   value = round(shift_val, 2)))
  }

  final_mean <- as.numeric(mean_val) - shift_val
  final_var <- as.numeric(var_val)
  final_ci <- as.numeric(ci_95) - shift_val
  
  list(
    model = toupper(dist),
    fit_obj = fit,
    shift = shift_val,
    raw_params_df = raw_params,
    moments = c(mean=final_mean, var=final_var, ci95=final_ci),
    aic = AIC(fit),
    bic = BIC(fit)
  )
}

# helper to generate plot data for incubation (MLE page)
get_plot_data_inc <- function(data, fit_res) {
  h_breaks <- seq(floor(min(data))-0.5, ceiling(max(data))+0.5, by = 1)
  hist_data <- hist(data, plot = FALSE, breaks = h_breaks)
  
  hist_df <- data.frame(
    from = hist_data$breaks[-length(hist_data$breaks)],
    to = hist_data$breaks[-1],
    y = hist_data$density,
    x = hist_data$mids
  )
  
  est <- fit_res$fit_obj$estimate
  d_name <- tolower(fit_res$model)
  min_x_calc <- max(0.01, min(data) - 1.5)
  x_vals <- seq(min_x_calc, max(data) + 1.5, length.out = 500)
  
  suppressWarnings({
    y_vals <- tryCatch({
      switch(d_name,
             "lognormal" = dlnorm(x_vals, meanlog = est["meanlog"], sdlog = est["sdlog"]),
             "weibull" = dweibull(x_vals, shape = est["shape"], scale = est["scale"]),
             "gamma"  = dgamma(x_vals, shape = est["shape"], rate = est["rate"])
      )
    }, error = function(e) return(rep(0, length(x_vals))))
  })
  
  curve_data <- data.frame(x = x_vals, y = y_vals)
  list(hist = hist_df, curve = curve_data)
}

# helper to generate plot data for serial interval (MLE page)
get_plot_data_si <- function(data, fit_res) {
  h_breaks <- seq(floor(min(data))-1, ceiling(max(data))+1, by = 2) 
  hist_data <- hist(data, plot = FALSE, breaks = h_breaks)
  hist_df <- data.frame(from = hist_data$breaks[-length(hist_data$breaks)], to = hist_data$breaks[-1], y = hist_data$density, x = hist_data$mids)
  
  # the shift the model was actually fitted with, so the curve lines up with
  # the histogram of the observed values
  shift_val <- if (!is.null(fit_res$shift)) fit_res$shift else
                 if (tolower(fit_res$model) == "normal") 0 else 1
  est <- fit_res$fit_obj$estimate
  d_name <- tolower(fit_res$model)
  x_vals <- seq(min(data) - 5, max(data) + 5, length.out = 500)
  x_trans <- x_vals + shift_val
  
  if(shift_val > 0) x_trans[x_trans <= 0] <- NA
  
  suppressWarnings({
    y_vals <- tryCatch({
      switch(d_name,
             "lognormal" = dlnorm(x_trans, meanlog = est["meanlog"], sdlog = est["sdlog"]),
             "weibull"   = dweibull(x_trans, shape = est["shape"], scale = est["scale"]),
             "gamma"     = dgamma(x_trans, shape = est["shape"], rate = est["rate"]),
             "normal"    = dnorm(x_trans, mean = est["mean"], sd = est["sd"])
      )
    }, error = function(e) return(rep(0, length(x_vals))))
  })
  y_vals[is.na(y_vals)] <- 0
  curve_data <- data.frame(x = x_vals, y = y_vals)
  list(hist = hist_df, curve = curve_data)
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# bayesian models: stan source and compilation
#
# the stan code below is the only definition of the four bayesian models. a
# compiled stan model is a shared library that loads only on the platform, R
# version and rstan version that built it, so a binary built elsewhere fails
# with "the compiled object from C++ code for this model is invalid".
#
# a model is taken from, in this order:
#   1. this R session, once it has been loaded
#   2. the per-user cache (see stan_cache_dir), filled by an earlier compilation
#      on this computer
#   3. the stan_models folder of the app, filled by precompile_models.R --bundle
#      on a computer with the same platform, R version and rstan version
#   4. a compilation on this computer, in a separate R process. that process
#      starts when the app opens and works through the models one at a time,
#      the one the user is waiting for first, so the first run seldom waits for
#      the whole compilation and the app shows how long it has been going.
#
# a binary is used only when it was built for this platform and from the source
# in get_stan_code(), so the code shown here and the code that produced the
# results can never drift apart. compiling takes one to three minutes and about
# 3.5 GB of memory per model, which is why only one model is compiled at a time.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- stan helpers: start ------------------------------------------------
# precompile_models.R and the background compilation both read the block
# between these two markers, so the models stay defined in exactly one place.
# please keep them in place.

STAN_MODELS <- c("Lognormal", "Weibull", "Gamma", "Normal")

# bayesian helper: the stan source each model is built from
get_stan_code <- function(model_name = "Weibull") {

  if (model_name == "Weibull") {
    return("
data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  vector[N] tStartExposure;
  vector[N] tEndExposure;
  vector[N] tSymptomOnset;
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0> alphaInc; // shape
  real<lower=0> sigmaInc; // scale
  vector<lower=0, upper=1>[N] uE;
}
transformed parameters {
  vector[N] tE;
  tE = tStartExposure + uE .* (tEndExposure - tStartExposure);
}
model {
  // priors
  alphaInc ~ lognormal(log(2.0), 1.0);
  sigmaInc ~ lognormal(log(3.0), 1.0);

  // likelihood
  target += weibull_lpdf((tSymptomOnset - tE) + 0.1 | alphaInc, sigmaInc);
}
")
  }
  else if (model_name == "Gamma") {
    return("
data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  vector[N] tStartExposure;
  vector[N] tEndExposure;
  vector[N] tSymptomOnset;
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0> alphaInc; // shape
  real<lower=0> sigmaInc; // rate
  vector<lower=0, upper=1>[N] uE;
}
transformed parameters {
  vector[N] tE;
  tE = tStartExposure + uE .* (tEndExposure - tStartExposure);
}
model {
  // priors
  alphaInc ~ lognormal(log(2.0), 1.0);
  sigmaInc ~ lognormal(log(0.66), 1.0);

  // likelihood
  target += gamma_lpdf((tSymptomOnset - tE) + 0.1 | alphaInc, sigmaInc);
}
")
  }
  else if (model_name == "Lognormal") {
    return("
data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  vector[N] tStartExposure;
  vector[N] tEndExposure;
  vector[N] tSymptomOnset;
}
parameters {
  real alphaInc;          // meanlog
  real<lower=0> sigmaInc; // sdlog
  vector<lower=0, upper=1>[N] uE;
}
transformed parameters {
  vector[N] tE;
  tE = tStartExposure + uE .* (tEndExposure - tStartExposure);
}
model {
  // priors
  alphaInc ~ normal(log(3.0), 1.0);
  sigmaInc ~ normal(0, 1.0);

  // likelihood
  target += lognormal_lpdf((tSymptomOnset - tE) + 0.1 | alphaInc, sigmaInc);
}
")
  }
  else if (model_name == "Normal") {
    return("
data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  vector[N] tStartExposure;
  vector[N] tEndExposure;
  vector[N] tSymptomOnset;
}
parameters {
  real alphaInc;          // mean
  real<lower=0> sigmaInc; // sd
  vector<lower=0, upper=1>[N] uE;
}
transformed parameters {
  vector[N] tE;
  tE = tStartExposure + uE .* (tEndExposure - tStartExposure);
}
model {
  // priors
  alphaInc ~ normal(3.0, 1.0);
  sigmaInc ~ normal(0, 1.0);

  // likelihood
  target += normal_lpdf((tSymptomOnset - tE) + 0.1 | alphaInc, sigmaInc);
}
")
  }
  return(NULL)
}

# where the models compiled on this computer are kept. set EPIPARAM_STAN_CACHE
# to place them somewhere else, for example on a shared server installation.
stan_cache_dir <- function() {
  d <- Sys.getenv("EPIPARAM_STAN_CACHE", "")
  if (!nzchar(d)) {
    d <- tryCatch(tools::R_user_dir("EpiParam", "cache"),
                  error = function(e) file.path(tempdir(), "EpiParam-stan"))
  }
  dir.create(d, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  d
}

# the file name carries the platform, the rstan version and the R version, so a
# binary is never handed to an installation that cannot load it. R keeps
# compiled code compatible within a minor version (4.4.0 to 4.4.3, say), so the
# R version is given as major.minor.
stan_model_file_name <- function(model_name) {
  r_minor <- strsplit(R.version$minor, ".", fixed = TRUE)[[1]][1]
  sprintf("%s-%s-rstan%s-R%s.%s.rds", tolower(model_name), R.version$platform,
          utils::packageVersion("rstan"), R.version$major, r_minor)
}

stan_cache_file <- function(model_name) {
  file.path(stan_cache_dir(), stan_model_file_name(model_name))
}

# models built in advance with precompile_models.R --bundle and shipped in the
# stan_models folder next to the app
stan_bundle_file <- function(model_name) {
  file.path("stan_models", stan_model_file_name(model_name))
}

# stan source reduced to what matters for a comparison: rstan normalises the
# code it stores (it drops blank lines), so the two are compared without blank
# lines or trailing spaces rather than character by character
stan_code_key <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("\r\n", "\n", as.character(x), fixed = TRUE)
  lines <- trimws(strsplit(x, "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
  paste(lines[nzchar(lines)], collapse = "\n")
}

# a compiled object is safe to use only if it was built for this platform and
# from the source the app is asking for
stan_model_usable <- function(mod, code) {
  if (!inherits(mod, "stanmodel")) return(FALSE)
  if (!identical(stan_code_key(mod@model_code), stan_code_key(code))) return(FALSE)
  built_on <- tryCatch(mod@dso@system, error = function(e) NA_character_)
  if (!identical(built_on, paste(R.version$arch, R.version$os, sep = ", "))) return(FALSE)
  # rstan's own check as well, where it is available: it also catches a dso
  # that is no longer loaded
  isTRUE(tryCatch(rstan:::is_sm_valid(mod), error = function(e) TRUE))
}

# the model saved in a file, or NULL when there is none this installation can
# use. a cached file that cannot be used (older source, another installation)
# is removed so that it gets rebuilt.
stan_read_model <- function(path, code, remove_stale = FALSE) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(NULL)
  mod <- tryCatch(readRDS(path), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (stan_model_usable(mod, code)) return(mod)
  if (remove_stale) unlink(path)
  NULL
}

# a model being compiled is marked by a folder next to its cache file. creating
# a folder either succeeds or fails as a whole, so two R processes never both
# start compiling the same model.
stan_lock_dir <- function(model_name) paste0(stan_cache_file(model_name), ".lock")

# the compiler's message from a failed attempt, kept for the app to show
stan_error_file <- function(model_name) paste0(stan_cache_file(model_name), ".error")

# is an R process on this computer compiling the model right now? a lock left
# behind by a process that stopped part way is removed.
stan_lock_busy <- function(model_name) {
  lock <- stan_lock_dir(model_name)
  if (!dir.exists(lock)) return(FALSE)
  age <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), file.mtime(lock), units = "secs"))
  pid <- tryCatch(as.integer(readLines(file.path(lock, "pid"), warn = FALSE)[1]),
                  error = function(e) NA_integer_, warning = function(w) NA_integer_)
  busy <- if (is.na(pid)) {
    age < 30                                   # just created, pid not written yet
  } else if (requireNamespace("ps", quietly = TRUE)) {
    age < 1800 && isTRUE(tryCatch(ps::ps_is_running(ps::ps_handle(pid)),
                                  error = function(e) FALSE))
  } else {
    age < 900
  }
  if (!busy) unlink(lock, recursive = TRUE)
  busy
}

stan_lock_take <- function(model_name) {
  if (stan_lock_busy(model_name)) return(FALSE)
  lock <- stan_lock_dir(model_name)
  if (!dir.create(lock, showWarnings = FALSE)) {
    # either another process got there first, or the cache folder cannot be
    # written to, in which case compile anyway
    return(!dir.exists(lock))
  }
  writeLines(as.character(Sys.getpid()), file.path(lock, "pid"))
  TRUE
}

# compile a model into the cache, unless a usable copy exists already or
# another process is compiling it. run by the background process and by
# precompile_models.R. returns TRUE when a usable model is in place.
stan_build <- function(model_name) {
  code  <- get_stan_code(model_name)
  cache <- stan_cache_file(model_name)
  if (!is.null(stan_read_model(cache, code, remove_stale = TRUE)) ||
      !is.null(stan_read_model(stan_bundle_file(model_name), code))) {
    return(invisible(TRUE))
  }
  if (!stan_lock_take(model_name)) return(invisible(FALSE))
  on.exit(unlink(stan_lock_dir(model_name), recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  unlink(stan_error_file(model_name))
  message("compiling the ", tolower(model_name), " model for this computer")
  mod <- tryCatch(
    rstan::stan_model(model_code = code,
                      model_name = paste0("epiparam_", tolower(model_name))),
    error = function(e) {
      # rstan's own message says little; the end of the compiler output, which
      # the background process writes to a log, says what went wrong
      log <- Sys.getenv("EPIPARAM_STAN_LOG")
      out <- if (nzchar(log) && file.exists(log)) tail(readLines(log, warn = FALSE), 15)
      try(writeLines(c(conditionMessage(e), out), stan_error_file(model_name)), silent = TRUE)
      NULL
    }
  )
  if (is.null(mod)) return(invisible(FALSE))
  # saved under a temporary name first, so no one ever reads a half-written file
  part <- paste0(cache, ".part", Sys.getpid())
  saved <- !inherits(try(saveRDS(mod, part), silent = TRUE), "try-error") &&
    file.rename(part, cache)
  unlink(part)
  invisible(saved)
}

# the text of this block, so that a separate R process can define the same
# functions. taken from the chunk while the app is being knitted, otherwise
# from the application file in the working folder.
stan_helpers_text <- function() {
  src <- tryCatch(unlist(knitr::knit_code$get("setup-chunk")), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!any(grepl("^# --- stan helpers: end", src))) {
    for (f in list.files(".", pattern = "[.]Rmd$")) {
      s <- readLines(f, warn = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8")
      if (any(grepl("^# --- stan helpers: end", s))) { src <- s; break }
    }
  }
  i0 <- grep("^# --- stan helpers: start", src)
  i1 <- grep("^# --- stan helpers: end", src)
  if (length(i0) != 1 || length(i1) != 1 || i1 <= i0) return(NULL)
  paste(src[(i0 + 1):(i1 - 1)], collapse = "\n")
}

# the background process of this R session, if one has been started
stan_job <- function() get0(".epiparam_stan_job", envir = .GlobalEnv, inherits = FALSE)

# while the background process works through its list, the model a user is
# waiting for is written here and compiled next
stan_next_file <- function() {
  file.path(stan_cache_dir(), sprintf("next-%s.txt", Sys.getpid()))
}

# start a separate R process that compiles the models, one at a time. returns
# FALSE when that is not possible (callr missing, or the cache folder cannot be
# written to).
stan_start_build <- function(models) {
  if (!requireNamespace("callr", quietly = TRUE)) return(FALSE)
  if (file.access(stan_cache_dir(), 2) != 0) return(FALSE)
  helpers <- if (exists("STAN_HELPERS_TEXT") && !is.null(STAN_HELPERS_TEXT)) {
    STAN_HELPERS_TEXT
  } else {
    stan_helpers_text()
  }
  if (is.null(helpers)) return(FALSE)
  log <- tempfile("compile-", tmpdir = stan_cache_dir(), fileext = ".log")
  job <- tryCatch(
    callr::r_bg(
      function(helpers, models, cache, next_file, log) {
        Sys.setenv(EPIPARAM_STAN_CACHE = cache, EPIPARAM_STAN_LOG = log)
        eval(parse(text = helpers), envir = globalenv())
        on.exit(unlink(c(next_file, log)), add = TRUE)
        todo <- models
        while (length(todo)) {
          wanted <- tryCatch(readLines(next_file, warn = FALSE)[1],
                             error = function(e) NA, warning = function(w) NA)
          m <- if (!is.na(wanted) && wanted %in% todo) wanted else todo[1]
          todo <- setdiff(todo, m)
          stan_build(m)
        }
      },
      args = list(helpers = helpers, models = models, cache = stan_cache_dir(),
                  next_file = stan_next_file(), log = log),
      # stopped, with the compiler it started, when the app stops
      stdout = log, stderr = "2>&1", supervise = TRUE, cleanup_tree = TRUE
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(job)) return(FALSE)
  assign(".epiparam_stan_job", job, envir = .GlobalEnv)
  TRUE
}

# when the app opens: start compiling, in the background, the models this
# computer does not have yet, the default model of each bayesian page first.
# set EPIPARAM_STAN_PREPARE=false to switch this off.
stan_prepare_models <- function(models = c("Lognormal", "Normal", "Weibull", "Gamma")) {
  if (identical(tolower(Sys.getenv("EPIPARAM_STAN_PREPARE")), "false")) return(invisible(FALSE))
  job <- stan_job()
  if (!is.null(job) && job$is_alive()) return(invisible(TRUE))
  have <- file.exists(vapply(models, stan_cache_file, "")) |
    file.exists(vapply(models, stan_bundle_file, ""))
  if (all(have)) return(invisible(FALSE))
  invisible(stan_start_build(models))
}

# progress note, shown in the app while it is running and on the console otherwise
stan_note <- function(msg, console = TRUE) {
  if (requireNamespace("shiny", quietly = TRUE) &&
      !is.null(shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain())) {
    try(shiny::setProgress(detail = msg), silent = TRUE)
  } else if (console) {
    message(msg)
  }
}

stan_elapsed <- function(secs) {
  secs <- max(0, round(as.numeric(secs)))
  if (secs < 60) paste(secs, "s") else sprintf("%d min %02d s", secs %/% 60, secs %% 60)
}

# wait until the model is compiled, starting the compilation if no one has, and
# keep the user informed meanwhile. returns FALSE when no separate process could
# be used, so the caller compiles in this R session instead.
stan_wait_for_model <- function(model_name) {
  cache   <- stan_cache_file(model_name)
  started <- Sys.time()
  own     <- FALSE
  tick    <- 0
  repeat {
    busy <- stan_lock_busy(model_name)
    if (!busy && file.exists(cache)) return(TRUE)
    # a compilation never takes this long: stop waiting and compile here
    if (difftime(Sys.time(), started, units = "mins") > 20) return(FALSE)
    on_console <- tick %% 15 == 0
    tick <- tick + 1
    job <- stan_job()
    job_alive <- !is.null(job) && job$is_alive()
    if (busy) {
      since <- tryCatch(file.mtime(stan_lock_dir(model_name)), error = function(e) started)
      stan_note(paste0("compiling the ", tolower(model_name), " model for this computer ",
                       "(first run only, usually one to three minutes): ",
                       stan_elapsed(difftime(Sys.time(), since, units = "secs"))), on_console)
    } else if (job_alive) {
      # the background process is busy with another model: this one is next
      try(writeLines(model_name, stan_next_file()), silent = TRUE)
      other <- Filter(stan_lock_busy, setdiff(STAN_MODELS, model_name))
      stan_note(paste0(if (length(other)) paste0("finishing the ", tolower(other[1]), " model; ") else "",
                       "the ", tolower(model_name), " model is compiled next (first run only): ",
                       stan_elapsed(difftime(Sys.time(), started, units = "secs"))), on_console)
    } else if (own) {
      return(TRUE)    # the compilation ended without a model; the caller reports why
    } else {
      if (!stan_start_build(model_name)) return(FALSE)
      own <- TRUE
    }
    Sys.sleep(1)
  }
}

# what to tell the user when the machine has no working C++ toolchain
stan_build_help <- function(model_name, err) {
  paste0(
    "The ", model_name, " model could not be compiled on this computer.\n\n",
    "EpiParam builds the Bayesian models the first time they are used, and that needs\n",
    "a working C++ toolchain:\n",
    "  Windows   install Rtools from https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/\n",
    "  macOS     run  xcode-select --install  in the Terminal\n",
    "  Linux     install the build tools, for example  sudo apt install build-essential\n\n",
    "Restart R once it is installed, then run the model again.\n\n",
    "The compiler reported:\n", err
  )
}

# the compiled model, from wherever it is available (see the notes above)
get_compiled_stan_model <- function(model_name = "Weibull") {

  code <- get_stan_code(model_name)
  if (is.null(code)) stop("unknown bayesian model: ", model_name, call. = FALSE)

  obj_name <- paste0("stan_model_", model_name)
  keep <- function(mod) {
    assign(obj_name, mod, envir = .GlobalEnv)
    mod
  }

  # already loaded in this session
  if (exists(obj_name, envir = .GlobalEnv)) {
    mod <- get(obj_name, envir = .GlobalEnv)
    if (stan_model_usable(mod, code)) return(mod)
  }

  # compiled on this computer before, or shipped with the app for this installation
  mod <- stan_read_model(stan_cache_file(model_name), code, remove_stale = TRUE)
  if (is.null(mod)) mod <- stan_read_model(stan_bundle_file(model_name), code)
  if (!is.null(mod)) return(keep(mod))

  # otherwise it is compiled here, in a separate R process where possible
  if (stan_wait_for_model(model_name)) {
    mod <- stan_read_model(stan_cache_file(model_name), code)
    if (!is.null(mod)) return(keep(mod))
    err <- tryCatch(paste(readLines(stan_error_file(model_name), warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n"),
                    error = function(e) NULL, warning = function(w) NULL)
    if (!is.null(err)) stop(stan_build_help(model_name, err), call. = FALSE)
  }

  # and in this R session when that is not possible
  stan_note(paste0("compiling the ", tolower(model_name),
                   " model for this computer (first run only, usually one to three minutes)"))
  mod <- tryCatch(
    rstan::stan_model(model_code = code,
                      model_name = paste0("epiparam_", tolower(model_name))),
    error = function(e) stop(stan_build_help(model_name, conditionMessage(e)), call. = FALSE)
  )
  try(saveRDS(mod, stan_cache_file(model_name)), silent = TRUE)
  keep(mod)
}

# --- stan helpers: end --------------------------------------------------

# the block above as text, for the separate R process that compiles the models
STAN_HELPERS_TEXT <- stan_helpers_text()
```

```{r inc-data-processing}

# incubation data processing pipeline

dataset_inc <- eventReactive(list(input$file1_inc, input$sex_inc, input$age_group_inc), {
  req(input$file1_inc)
  
  dataset <- read.csv(input$file1_inc$datapath)
  dataset <- data.frame(lapply(dataset, trimws), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  dataset <- clean_names(dataset)
  
  # validation start
  validate(
    need(all(c("date_of_exposure", "date_of_onset") %in% names(dataset)),
         "incorrect dataset: please upload the incubation data containing 'date of exposure' and 'date of onset'.")
  )
  # validation end
  
  if("sex" %in% names(dataset)) {
    dataset <- dataset %>%
      mutate(sex = case_when(
        grepl("^m", sex, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Male",
        grepl("^f", sex, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Female",
        TRUE ~ sex
      ))
  }
  
  if("age_group" %in% names(dataset)) {
    dataset$age_group <- dataset$age_group %>%
      trimws() %>%              
      gsub("s$", "", ., ignore.case = TRUE) %>%
      gsub("[^0-9]", "", .)
    dataset$age_group <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(dataset$age_group))
    dataset <- dataset %>% mutate(age_group = case_when(
      age_group > 0 & age_group <= 19 ~ '0 - 19',
      age_group >= 20 & age_group <= 29 ~ '20 - 29',
      age_group >= 30 & age_group <= 39 ~ '30 - 39',
      age_group >= 40 & age_group <= 49 ~ '40 - 49',
      age_group >= 50 & age_group <= 59 ~ '50 - 59',
      TRUE ~ '≥ 60'
    ))
  }
  
  if (input$sex_inc != "All") dataset <- dataset %>% filter(sex == input$sex_inc)
  if (input$age_group_inc != "All") dataset <- dataset %>% filter(age_group == input$age_group_inc)
  
  dataset
})

# every row of the selection, with the dates as the app read them and a note of
# what became of it. the preview, the check panel and the model all read this,
# so what the user is shown is what the model was given.
inc_checked <- reactive({
  req(dataset_inc())
  d <- dataset_inc()
  d$exposure_read   <- parse_date(d$date_of_exposure)
  d$onset_read      <- parse_date(d$date_of_onset)
  d$incubation_days <- as.numeric(d$onset_read - d$exposure_read)
  d$status <- dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(d$exposure_read) & is.na(d$onset_read) ~ "excluded: neither date could be read",
    is.na(d$exposure_read)                       ~ "excluded: exposure date could not be read",
    is.na(d$onset_read)                          ~ "excluded: onset date could not be read",
    d$incubation_days <= 0                       ~ "excluded: onset falls on or before exposure",
    TRUE                                         ~ "used"
  )
  d
})

get_incu_data <- function() {
  d <- inc_checked()
  data <- d$incubation_days[d$status == "used"]
  data <- data[!is.na(data)]
  if(length(data) == 0) return(NULL)
  data
}

# master fitting logic for incubation
fit_results_inc <- reactive({
  data <- get_incu_data()
  if (is.null(data) || length(data) < 3) return(NULL)
  
  models <- if(input$model_inc == "ALL") c("lognormal", "weibull", "gamma") else tolower(input$model_inc)
  
  res <- list()
  for(m in models) {
    # fit logic
    suppressWarnings({
      fit <- fit_parametric_model(data, m, shift_val = 0)
    })
    if(!is.null(fit)) res[[m]] <- fit
  }
  res
})
```

### Model Fit Statistics

```{r inc-fit-stats}

renderDT({
  res <- fit_results_inc()
  data <- get_incu_data()
  
  if (!is.null(data) && length(data) < 3) {
    df <- data.frame(Status = paste("Insufficient data points (N=", length(data), "). Need 3+ incubation period data points."))
  } else if (is.null(res) || length(res) == 0) {
    df <- data.frame(Status = "No data or fit failed")
  } else {
    if (input$model_inc != "ALL") {
      df <- res[[1]]$raw_params_df
    } else {
      df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(res, function(x) {
        data.frame(
          Model = x$model, 
          AIC = round(x$aic, 2), 
          BIC = round(x$bic, 2)
        )
      }))
      df <- df[order(df$AIC), ] 
    }
  }
  
  datatable(
    df, rownames = FALSE,
    options = list(
      dom = "Brt",
      buttons = list("csv", "excel", "pdf"),
      pageLength = nrow(df)
    ),
    extensions = "Buttons"
  ) %>% 
    formatStyle(columns = names(df), `font-size` = "12px") %>%
    formatStyle(columns = intersect(names(df), c("parameter", "Model")), fontWeight = "bold")
})
```

### Model Parameters

```{r inc-model-params}

renderDT({
  res <- fit_results_inc()
  data <- get_incu_data()
  
  if (!is.null(data) && length(data) < 3) {
    df <- data.frame(Status = "Insufficient Data")
  } else if (is.null(res) || length(res) == 0) {
    df <- data.frame(Status = "No data")
  } else {
    fmt_moments <- function(x) {
      data.frame(
        parameter = c(paste(x$model, "Mean"), paste(x$model, "Variance"), "95th Percentile"),
        value = round(c(x$moments["mean"], x$moments["var"], x$moments["ci95"]), 3)
      )
    }
    
    if (input$model_inc != "ALL") {
      df <- fmt_moments(res[[1]])
    } else {
      df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(res, function(x) {
        data.frame(
          Model = x$model,
          `Mean` = round(x$moments["mean"], 3),
          `Variance` = round(x$moments["var"], 3),
          `95th Percentile` = round(x$moments["ci95"], 3),
          check.names = FALSE
        )
      }))
    }
  }
  
  datatable(
    df, rownames = FALSE,
    options = list(
      dom = "Brt",
      buttons = list("csv", "excel", "pdf"),
      pageLength = nrow(df)
    ),
    extensions = "Buttons"
  ) %>% 
    formatStyle(columns = names(df), `font-size` = "12px") %>%
    formatStyle(columns = intersect(names(df), c("parameter", "Model")), fontWeight = "bold")
})
```

```{r inc-histograms}
renderHighchart({
  data <- get_incu_data()
  res <- fit_results_inc()
  
  if (is.null(data) || length(data) < 3 || is.null(res) || length(res) == 0) {
    return(highchart() %>% hc_title(text="Insufficient Data (N < 3)"))
  }
  
  col_map <- list(lognormal="#00BFFF", weibull="#FF8C00", gamma="#228B22")
  line_col_overlaid <- list(lognormal="#000000", weibull="#FF0000", gamma="#008000") 
  
  # style definitions
  axis_style <- list(color = "#000000", fontSize = "16px", fontWeight = "bold")
  label_style <- list(color = "#000000", fontSize = "14px", fontWeight = "bold")
  menu_items <- list("viewFullscreen", "separator", "downloadPNG", "downloadPDF", "downloadSVG")
  
  if (input$model_inc == "ALL") {
    
    # calculate global max y for constant scale
    max_y <- 0
    all_plot_data <- list()
    for(m in names(res)) {
      pd <- get_plot_data_inc(data, res[[m]])
      local_max <- max(c(pd$hist$y, pd$curve$y), na.rm = TRUE)
      if(local_max > max_y) max_y <- local_max
      all_plot_data[[m]] <- pd
    }
    max_y <- max_y * 1.05
    
    # sub-case a: overlaid (combined) view
    if (input$view_inc == "Overlaid") {
      pd <- all_plot_data[[1]] # base hist data
      
      hc <- highchart() %>%

        hc_title(text = "Combined Model Comparison", style = list(fontSize="16px", fontWeight="bold")) %>%
        hc_plotOptions(
          series = list(pointPlacement = "on"), # fix for axis alignment
          column = list(grouping = FALSE, pointPadding = 0, groupPadding = 0, borderWidth = 0.25)
        ) %>%
        hc_xAxis(

          lineColor = "#000000", lineWidth = 1, tickWidth = 1, tickColor = "#000000",

          labels = list(style = label_style),

        ) %>%
        # add histogram

      # add curves

    } else {

        ) %>%

        ) %>%
```

```{r inc-bayes-data-processing}

# global data loading (runs once per file upload)
bayes_inc_global <- reactive({
  req(input$file_bayes_inc)
  
  # robust read
  tryCatch({
    df <- read.csv(input$file_bayes_inc$datapath, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }, error = function(e) {
    validate(need(FALSE, "error reading file. please ensure it is a valid csv."))
  })
  
  df <- clean_names(df) 
  
  # validation start
  validate(
    need(all(c("symptom_onset", "exp_date_min", "exp_date_max") %in% names(df)),
         "incorrect dataset: please upload incubation bayesian data containing 'symptom onset', 'exp date min', and 'exp date max'.")
  )
  # validation end
  
  # standardize sex
  if("sex" %in% names(df)) {
    df <- df %>% mutate(sex = case_when(
        grepl("^m", sex, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Male",
        grepl("^f", sex, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Female",
        TRUE ~ sex
      ))
  }
  
  # standardize age group
  if("age" %in% names(df)) {
    df$age <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(df$age))
    df <- df %>% mutate(age_group = case_when(
      age > 0 & age <= 19 ~ '0 - 19',
      age >= 20 & age <= 29 ~ '20 - 29',
      age >= 30 & age <= 39 ~ '30 - 39',
      age >= 40 & age <= 49 ~ '40 - 49',
      age >= 50 & age <= 59 ~ '50 - 59',
      TRUE ~ '≥ 60'
    ))
  }
  
  # parse dates globally
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      date_symp = parse_date(symptom_onset),
      date_min  = parse_date(exp_date_min),
      date_max  = parse_date(exp_date_max)
    )
  
  df
})

# filtering logic
bayes_inc_data <- reactive({
  req(bayes_inc_global())
  df <- bayes_inc_global()
  
  # filter raw data
  if (input$sex_bayes_inc != "All" && "sex" %in% names(df)) {
    df <- df %>% filter(sex == input$sex_bayes_inc)
  }
  if (input$age_bayes_inc != "All" && "age_group" %in% names(df)) {
    df <- df %>% filter(age_group == input$age_bayes_inc)
  }
  
  # capture count before cleaning
  n_before_cleaning <- nrow(df)
  
  # model prep logic
  df <- df %>%
    filter(!is.na(date_symp)) %>% # must have symptom date
    mutate(
      tSymptomOnset = as.integer(date_symp - as.Date("2019-12-31")),
      tStartExposure = as.integer(date_min - as.Date("2019-12-31")),
      tEndExposure = as.integer(date_max - as.Date("2019-12-31"))
    ) %>%
    # logic update!!
    # keep rows with at least one exposure date
    filter(!is.na(tStartExposure) | !is.na(tEndExposure)) %>%
    # impute missing end date (assume exposure continued until symptoms)
    mutate(tEndExposure = ifelse(is.na(tEndExposure), tSymptomOnset, tEndExposure)) %>%
    # impute missing start date (assume exposure started 14 days before end date)
    mutate(tStartExposure = ifelse(is.na(tStartExposure), tEndExposure, tStartExposure)) %>% # you can update the window here
    # final safety check: end exposure cannot be after symptoms
    mutate(tEndExposure = ifelse(tEndExposure > tSymptomOnset, tSymptomOnset, tEndExposure)) %>%
    # ensure start is before end
    filter(tStartExposure <= tEndExposure)
  
  # capture count after
  n_final <- nrow(df)
  n_dropped <- n_before_cleaning - n_final
  
  # notify user
  if (n_dropped > 0) {
    showNotification(
      paste0("data loaded: ", n_final, " valid rows used. (", n_dropped, " rows removed: missing both exposure dates or invalid timeline)"),
      type = "warning",
      duration = 5 
    )
  } else {
    showNotification(
      paste0("data successfully loaded: ", n_final, " rows ready."),
      type = "message",
      duration = 3 
    )
  }
  
  df
})

# every row of the selection, with the dates as the app read them, the exposure
# window it ended up using and a note of what became of the row. this repeats
# the preparation the model does, so the preview shows the model's own view of
# the file rather than the raw text.
bayes_inc_checked <- reactive({
  req(bayes_inc_global())
  d <- bayes_inc_global()
  if (input$sex_bayes_inc != "All" && "sex" %in% names(d)) {
    d <- d %>% filter(sex == input$sex_bayes_inc)
  }
  if (input$age_bayes_inc != "All" && "age_group" %in% names(d)) {
    d <- d %>% filter(age_group == input$age_bayes_inc)
  }
  
  origin <- as.Date("2019-12-31")
  tS <- as.integer(d$date_symp - origin)
  tB <- as.integer(d$date_min  - origin)
  tE <- as.integer(d$date_max  - origin)
  tE <- ifelse(is.na(tE), tS, tE)          # no end date: exposure ran to onset
  tB <- ifelse(is.na(tB), tE, tB)          # no start date: window has no width
  tE <- ifelse(tE > tS, tS, tE)            # exposure cannot end after onset
  
  d$onset_read           <- d$date_symp
  d$exposure_from        <- d$date_min
  d$exposure_to          <- d$date_max
  d$exposure_window_days <- tE - tB
  d$days_to_onset        <- tS - tE
  d$status <- dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(d$date_symp)                    ~ "excluded: symptom onset date could not be read",
    is.na(d$date_min) & is.na(d$date_max) ~ "excluded: no exposure date given",
    tB > tE                               ~ "excluded: exposure window ends before it starts",
    TRUE                                  ~ "used"
  )
  d
})

# modeling
bayes_inc_fit <- eventReactive(input$run_bayes_inc, {
  
  # lock button
  shinyjs::disable("run_bayes_inc")
  
  # unlock button when done
  on.exit({
    shinyjs::enable("run_bayes_inc")
  })
  
  # double clean
  gc()
  gc() 
  
  req(bayes_inc_data())
  df <- bayes_inc_data()

  validate(
    need(nrow(df) >= 5, "insufficient data: you need at least 5 observations to run this model.")
  )

  stan_data <- list(
    N = nrow(df),
    tStartExposure = df$tStartExposure,
    tEndExposure = df$tEndExposure,
    tSymptomOnset = df$tSymptomOnset
  )

  withProgress(message = 'running bayesian model...', detail = 'initializing...', value = 0, {

    mod <- get_compiled_stan_model(input$bayes_model_select)
    incProgress(0.1, detail = "sampling chains...")

    fit <- rstan::sampling(
      object = mod,
      data = stan_data,
      chains = 4,
      cores = min(4, parallel::detectCores(), na.rm = TRUE),
      seed = STAN_SEED,
      iter = input$iter_count_inc,
      warmup = input$iter_count_inc / 2,
      refresh = 0,
      pars = c("alphaInc", "sigmaInc"), # keep light!
      control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95)
    )

    incProgress(0.8, detail = "extracting posteriors...")

    params <- rstan::extract(fit)

    list(
      fit_obj = fit,
      iterations = input$iter_count_inc,
      model_name = input$bayes_model_select,
      alpha = params$alphaInc,
      sigma = params$sigmaInc,
      alpha_summary = quantile(params$alphaInc, probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)),
      sigma_summary = quantile(params$sigmaInc, probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
    )
  })
})
```

### Model Statistics (Median & 95% CrI)

```{r inc-bayes-model-stats}

renderDT({
  req(bayes_inc_fit())
  res <- bayes_inc_fit()
  
  # dynamic parameter labels & mean calculation
  if (res$model_name == "Lognormal") {
    p_names <- c("MeanLog (Alpha)", "SDLog (Sigma)")
    # mean of lognormal = exp(mu + sigma^2/2)
    post_means <- exp(res$alpha + (res$sigma^2)/2)
  } else if (res$model_name == "Gamma") {
    p_names <- c("Shape (Alpha)", "Rate (Sigma)")
    # mean of gamma = shape / rate
    post_means <- res$alpha / res$sigma
  } else {
    # weibull
    p_names <- c("Shape (Alpha)", "Scale (Sigma)")
    # mean of weibull = scale * gamma(1 + 1/shape)
    post_means <- res$sigma * gamma(1 + 1/res$alpha)
  }
  
  df_stats <- data.frame(
    Parameter = p_names,
    `Median` = round(c(res$alpha_summary[2], res$sigma_summary[2]), 3),
    `Lower_95_CrI` = round(c(res$alpha_summary[1], res$sigma_summary[1]), 3),
    `Upper_95_CrI` = round(c(res$alpha_summary[3], res$sigma_summary[3]), 3)
  )
  
  mean_summ <- quantile(post_means, probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
  
  df_mean <- data.frame(
    Parameter = "Mean Incubation Period",
    `Median` = round(mean_summ[2], 3),
    `Lower_95_CrI` = round(mean_summ[1], 3),
    `Upper_95_CrI` = round(mean_summ[3], 3)
  )
  
  final_df <- rbind(df_stats, df_mean)
  
  fname <- paste0("Incubation_Bayesian_Stats_", Sys.Date())
  
  datatable(
    final_df, 
    rownames = FALSE, 
    extensions = 'Buttons',
    options = list(
      dom = 'Brt',
      buttons = list(
        list(extend = "csv", filename = fname),
        list(extend = "excel", filename = fname),
        list(extend = "pdf", filename = fname)
      ),
      columnDefs = list(list(className = 'dt-center', targets = "_all"))
    )
  ) %>%
    formatStyle(columns = "Parameter", fontWeight = "bold")
})
```

### Posterior Distribution (Median Fit)

```{r inc-bayes-posterior-dist}

renderHighchart({
  req(bayes_inc_fit())
  res <- bayes_inc_fit()
  
  alpha_est <- median(res$alpha)
  sigma_est <- median(res$sigma)
  x_vals <- seq(0, 30, length.out = 200)
  
  # dynamic distribution logic
  if (res$model_name == "Gamma") {
    y_vals <- dgamma(x_vals, shape = alpha_est, rate = sigma_est)
  } else if (res$model_name == "Lognormal") {
    y_vals <- dlnorm(x_vals, meanlog = alpha_est, sdlog = sigma_est)
  } else {
    y_vals <- dweibull(x_vals, shape = alpha_est, scale = sigma_est)
  }
  
  model_label <- tools::toTitleCase(res$model_name)
  menu_items <- list("viewFullscreen", "separator", "downloadPNG", "downloadPDF", "downloadSVG")
  
  # theme consistency
  axis_title_style <- list(color = "#000000", fontSize = "16px", fontWeight = "bold", fontFamily = "Jost")
  axis_label_style <- list(color = "#000000", fontSize = "14px", fontWeight = "bold", fontFamily = "Jost")
  
  highchart() %>%
    hc_chart(style = list(fontFamily = "Jost"), backgroundColor = "#FFFFFF") %>%
    
    hc_title(
      text = paste0("Posterior Predictive Distribution (", model_label, ")"),
      style = list(fontSize = "18px", fontWeight = "bold", fontFamily = "Jost", color = "#000000")
    ) %>%
    
    hc_subtitle(
      text = paste0("Based on ", res$iterations, " MCMC iterations"),
      style = list(fontSize = "14px", fontFamily = "Jost", color = "#666666")
    ) %>%
    
    hc_exporting(
      enabled = TRUE, 
      filename = paste0("Incubation_Posterior_Distribution_", Sys.Date()),
      buttons = list(contextButton = list(menuItems = menu_items))
    ) %>%
    
    hc_add_series(
      data = data.frame(x = x_vals, y = y_vals),
      type = "area",
      name = "Posterior Density",
      color = "rgba(65, 105, 225, 0.5)",
      marker = list(enabled = FALSE),      
      lineWidth = 2
    ) %>%
    
    # axis styling
    hc_xAxis(
      title = list(text = "Incubation Period (Days)", style = axis_title_style),
      labels = list(style = axis_label_style),
      min = 0, minPadding = 0, startOnTick = TRUE,
      lineColor = "#000000", lineWidth = 1, tickColor = "#000000"
    ) %>%
    
    hc_yAxis(
      title = list(text = "Density", style = axis_title_style),
      labels = list(style = axis_label_style),
      min = 0, minPadding = 0, startOnTick = TRUE,
      gridLineWidth = 0, 
      lineColor = "#000000", lineWidth = 1, tickColor = "#000000"
    ) %>%
    
    hc_tooltip(valueDecimals = 4, style = list(fontFamily = "Jost"))
})
```

```{r si-data-processing}

# data processing for serial interval
dataset_si <- eventReactive(list(input$file1_si, input$sex_si, input$age_group_si), {
  req(input$file1_si)
  
  dataset <- read.csv(input$file1_si$datapath)
  dataset <- data.frame(lapply(dataset, trimws), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  dataset <- clean_names(dataset)
  
  # validation start
  validate(
    need(all(c("id", "source_of_infection", "date_of_onset") %in% names(dataset)),
         "incorrect dataset: please upload serial interval data containing 'id', 'source of infection', and 'date of onset'.")
  )
  # validation end
  
  # more robust cleaning
  if("age_group" %in% names(dataset)) {
    dataset$age_group <- dataset$age_group %>%
      gsub("s$", "", ., ignore.case = TRUE) %>%
      gsub("[^0-9]", "", .)
    dataset$age_group <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(dataset$age_group))
    dataset <- dataset %>% mutate(age_group = case_when(
      age_group > 0 & age_group <= 19 ~ '0 - 19',
      age_group >= 20 & age_group <= 29 ~ '20 - 29',
      age_group >= 30 & age_group <= 39 ~ '30 - 39',
      age_group >= 40 & age_group <= 49 ~ '40 - 49',
      age_group >= 50 & age_group <= 59 ~ '50 - 59',
      TRUE ~ '≥ 60'
    ))
  }
  
  if("sex" %in% names(dataset)) {
    dataset <- dataset %>%
      mutate(sex = case_when(
        grepl("^m", sex, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Male",
        grepl("^f", sex, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Female",
        TRUE ~ sex
      ))
  }
  
  # keep what was typed, so the check panel can quote the values it could not use
  dataset$id_as_given     <- as.character(dataset$id)
  dataset$source_as_given <- as.character(dataset$source_of_infection)
  dataset$onset_as_given  <- as.character(dataset$date_of_onset)
  
  dataset$id <- as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9]", "", dataset$id))
  dataset$source_of_infection <- as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9]", "", dataset$source_of_infection))
  dataset$date_of_exposure <- parse_date(dataset$date_of_exposure)
  dataset$date_of_onset <- parse_date(dataset$date_of_onset)
  dataset$source_date <- dataset$date_of_onset[match(dataset$source_of_infection, dataset$id)]
  
  if (input$sex_si != "All") dataset <- dataset %>% filter(sex == input$sex_si)
  if (input$age_group_si != "All") dataset <- dataset %>% filter(age_group == input$age_group_si)
  
  dataset
})

# every row of the selection, with the serial interval the app worked out and a
# note of what became of it. a transmission link that points at a case which is
# not in the file is now reported instead of quietly disappearing.
si_checked <- reactive({
  req(dataset_si())
  d <- dataset_si()
  
  required_cols <- c("id", "source_of_infection", "date_of_onset", "source_date")
  if (!all(required_cols %in% names(d))) stop("required columns not found in dataset")
  
  d$serial_days <- as.numeric(d$date_of_onset - d$source_date)
  known_source  <- !is.na(d$source_of_infection) & d$source_of_infection %in% d$id
  d$status <- dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(d$date_of_onset)       ~ "excluded: onset date could not be read",
    is.na(d$source_of_infection) ~ "excluded: no source of infection given",
    !known_source                ~ "excluded: the source of infection is not one of the case ids in this file",
    is.na(d$source_date)         ~ "excluded: the source case has no readable onset date",
    TRUE                         ~ "used"
  )
  d
})

get_serial_data <- function() {
  d <- si_checked()
  v <- d$serial_days[d$status == "used"]
  v <- v[!is.na(v)]
  if (!length(v)) return(NULL)
  v
}

# master fitting logic for si
fit_results_si <- reactive({
  data <- get_serial_data()
  if (is.null(data) || length(data) < 3) return(NULL)
  
  models <- if(input$model_si == "ALL") c("normal", "weibull", "gamma", "lognormal") else tolower(input$model_si)
  
  res <- list()
  for(m in models) {
    # shift logic. weibull, gamma and lognormal are defined only for positive
    # values, so the serial intervals are moved to the right before fitting and
    # the fitted distribution is moved back afterwards, in fit_parametric_model.
    # the shift is taken from the data, k = 1 - min(si), so a negative serial
    # interval is kept instead of being dropped. with nothing negative k is 1,
    # which is what the app did before.
    shift_val <- if(m == "normal") 0 else max(1, 1 - min(data))
    
    # every value is positive after that shift; kept as a guard
    if(m != "normal") {
      valid_indices <- (data + shift_val) > 0
      data_for_fit <- data[valid_indices]
    } else {
      data_for_fit <- data
    }
    
    # check if we still have enough data after filtering
    if(length(data_for_fit) < 3) next
    
    suppressWarnings({
      fit <- fit_parametric_model(data_for_fit, m, shift_val = shift_val)
    })
    
    if(!is.null(fit)) res[[m]] <- fit
  }
  res
})

```

### Model Fit Statistics

```{r si-model-fit-stats}

renderDT({
  res <- fit_results_si()
  data <- get_serial_data()
  
  if (!is.null(data) && length(data) < 3) {
    df <- data.frame(Status = "Insufficient Data (N < 3).")
  } else if (is.null(res) || length(res) == 0) {
    df <- data.frame(Status = "No data or fit failed")
  } else {
    if (input$model_si != "ALL") {
      df <- res[[1]]$raw_params_df
    } else {
      df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(res, function(x) {
        data.frame(
          Model = x$model, 
          AIC = round(x$aic, 2), 
          BIC = round(x$bic, 2)
        )
      }))
      df <- df[order(df$AIC), ]
    }
  }
  
  datatable(
    df, rownames = FALSE,
    options = list(dom = "Brt", buttons = list("csv", "excel", "pdf"), pageLength = nrow(df)),
    extensions = "Buttons"
  ) %>% 
    formatStyle(columns = names(df), `font-size` = "12px") %>%
    formatStyle(columns = intersect(names(df), c("parameter", "Model")), fontWeight = "bold")
})

```

### Model Parameters

```{r si-model-params}

renderDT({
  res <- fit_results_si()
  data <- get_serial_data()
  
  if (!is.null(data) && length(data) < 3) {
    df <- data.frame(Status = "Insufficient Data")
  } else if (is.null(res) || length(res) == 0) {
    df <- data.frame(Status = "No data")
  } else {
    fmt_moments <- function(x) {
      data.frame(
        parameter = c(paste(x$model, "Mean"), paste(x$model, "Variance"), "95th Percentile"),
        value = round(c(x$moments["mean"], x$moments["var"], x$moments["ci95"]), 3)
      )
    }
    
    if (input$model_si != "ALL") {
      df <- fmt_moments(res[[1]])
    } else {
      df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(res, function(x) {
        data.frame(
          Model = x$model,
          `Mean` = round(x$moments["mean"], 3),
          `Variance` = round(x$moments["var"], 3),
          `95th Percentile` = round(x$moments["ci95"], 3),
          check.names = FALSE
        )
      }))
    }
  }
  
  datatable(
    df, rownames = FALSE,
    options = list(dom = "Brt", buttons = list("csv", "excel", "pdf"), pageLength = nrow(df)),
    extensions = "Buttons"
  ) %>% 
    formatStyle(columns = names(df), `font-size` = "12px") %>%
    formatStyle(columns = intersect(names(df), c("parameter", "Model")), fontWeight = "bold")
})
```

### Distribution Plots

```{r si-histograms}

renderHighchart({
  data <- get_serial_data()
  res <- fit_results_si()
  
  if (is.null(data) || length(data) < 3 || is.null(res) || length(res) == 0) {
    return(highchart() %>% hc_title(text="Insufficient Data (N < 3)"))
  }
  
  # set model colors
  col_map <- list(
    normal = "#DAA520",    # gold
    lognormal = "#00BFFF", # blue
    weibull = "#FF8C00",   # orange
    gamma = "#228B22"      # green
  )
  line_col_overlaid <- list(normal="#0000FF", lognormal="#000000", weibull="#FF0000", gamma="#008000")
  
  # style definitions
  axis_style <- list(color = "#000000", fontSize = "16px", fontWeight = "bold")
  label_style <- list(color = "#000000", fontSize = "14px", fontWeight = "bold")
  menu_items <- list("viewFullscreen", "separator", "downloadPNG", "downloadPDF", "downloadSVG")
  
  # ensure the first bar isn't cut in half (start x-axis slightly before min integer)
  min_x_val <- floor(min(data)) - 0.5
  
  # case 1: all models selected
  if (input$model_si == "ALL") {
    
    # calculate global max y
    max_y <- 0
    all_plot_data <- list()
    for(m in names(res)) {
      pd <- get_plot_data_si(data, res[[m]])
      local_max <- max(c(pd$hist$y, pd$curve$y), na.rm = TRUE)
      if(local_max > max_y) max_y <- local_max
      all_plot_data[[m]] <- pd
    }
    max_y <- max_y * 1.05
    
    # sub-case a: overlaid (combined) view
    if (input$view_si == "Overlaid") {
      
      pd <- all_plot_data[[1]] # base hist
      
      hc <- highchart() %>%
        hc_chart(type = "line", style = list(fontFamily = "Jost"), backgroundColor = "#FFFFFF") %>%
        hc_title(text = "Combined Model Comparison", style = list(fontSize="16px", fontWeight="bold")) %>%
        hc_plotOptions(
          series = list(pointPlacement = "on"), 
          column = list(grouping = FALSE, pointPadding = 0, groupPadding = 0, borderWidth = 0.25)
        ) %>%
        hc_xAxis(
          title = list(text = "Serial Interval (Days)", style = axis_style), 
          allowDecimals = FALSE, 
          lineColor = "#000000", lineWidth = 1, tickWidth = 1, tickColor = "#000000",
          labels = list(style = label_style),
          min = min_x_val, # Updated start point
          minPadding = 0, startOnTick = TRUE
        ) %>%
        hc_yAxis(
          title = list(text = "Density", style = axis_style), 
          gridLineWidth = 0, 
          lineWidth = 1, lineColor="#000000", tickWidth = 1, tickColor = "#000000",
          labels = list(style = label_style),
          min = 0, max = max_y, 
          minPadding = 0, startOnTick = TRUE
        ) %>%
        hc_add_series(
          data = list_parse(pd$hist), type = "column", name = "Observed Data",
          color = "#D3D3D3", borderColor = "#FFFFFF", borderWidth = 0.25,
          pointRange = 2, zIndex = 0
        )
      
      for(m in names(res)) {
        nm <- tolower(m)
        pd_model <- all_plot_data[[m]]
        hc <- hc %>% hc_add_series(
          data = pd_model$curve, type = "line", name = paste(m, "Fit"),
          color = line_col_overlaid[[nm]], lineWidth = 2, marker = list(enabled = FALSE), zIndex = 2
        )
      }
      hc <- hc %>% hc_exporting(enabled = TRUE, buttons = list(contextButton = list(menuItems = menu_items)))
      return(hc)
      
    } else {
      # sub-case b: side-by-side (composite) view with constant scale
      hc <- highchart() %>%
        hc_chart(type = "column", style = list(fontFamily = "Jost"), backgroundColor = "#FFFFFF") %>%
        hc_title(text = "Distribution Comparison", style = list(fontSize="16px", fontWeight="bold")) %>%
        hc_plotOptions(
          series = list(pointPlacement = "on"),
          column = list(grouping = FALSE, pointPadding = 0, groupPadding = 0, borderWidth = 0.25)
        ) %>%
        
        # 4 x-axes
        hc_xAxis_multiples(
          list(title = list(text = "Normal", style=axis_style), left = "0%", width = "22%", lineWidth=1, lineColor="black", tickWidth=1, tickColor="black", labels=list(style=label_style), min=min_x_val, minPadding=0, startOnTick=TRUE),
          list(title = list(text = "Weibull", style=axis_style), left = "26%", width = "22%", offset = 0, lineWidth=1, lineColor="black", tickWidth=1, tickColor="black", labels=list(style=label_style), min=min_x_val, minPadding=0, startOnTick=TRUE),
          list(title = list(text = "Gamma", style=axis_style), left = "52%", width = "22%", offset = 0, lineWidth=1, lineColor="black", tickWidth=1, tickColor="black", labels=list(style=label_style), min=min_x_val, minPadding=0, startOnTick=TRUE),
          list(title = list(text = "Lognormal", style=axis_style), left = "78%", width = "22%", offset = 0, lineWidth=1, lineColor="black", tickWidth=1, tickColor="black", labels=list(style=label_style), min=min_x_val, minPadding=0, startOnTick=TRUE)
        ) %>%
        
        # 4 y-axes (aligned, same scale)
        hc_yAxis_multiples(
          list(title = list(text = "Density", style=axis_style), left = "0%", width = "22%", lineWidth=1, lineColor="black", tickWidth=1, tickColor="black", gridLineWidth=0, labels=list(style=label_style), min=0, max=max_y, minPadding=0, startOnTick=TRUE),
          list(title = list(text = "Density", style=axis_style), left = "26%", width = "22%", offset = 0, lineWidth=1, lineColor="black", tickWidth=1, tickColor="black", gridLineWidth=0, labels=list(style=label_style), min=0, max=max_y, minPadding=0, startOnTick=TRUE),
          list(title = list(text = "Density", style=axis_style), left = "52%", width = "22%", offset = 0, lineWidth=1, lineColor="black", tickWidth=1, tickColor="black", gridLineWidth=0, labels=list(style=label_style), min=0, max=max_y, minPadding=0, startOnTick=TRUE),
          list(title = list(text = "Density", style=axis_style), left = "78%", width = "22%", offset = 0, lineWidth=1, lineColor="black", tickWidth=1, tickColor="black", gridLineWidth=0, labels=list(style=label_style), min=0, max=max_y, minPadding=0, startOnTick=TRUE)
        ) %>%
        
        hc_exporting(enabled = TRUE, buttons = list(contextButton = list(menuItems = menu_items)), chartOptions = list(chart = list(backgroundColor = "#FFFFFF"))) %>%
        hc_legend(enabled = FALSE)
      
      axes_idx <- list(normal=0, weibull=1, gamma=2, lognormal=3)
      for(m in names(res)) {
        nm <- tolower(m)
        idx <- axes_idx[[nm]]
        if(is.null(idx)) next 
        
        pd <- all_plot_data[[m]]
        
        hc <- hc %>%
          hc_add_series(
            data = list_parse(pd$hist), type = "column", color = col_map[[nm]],
            xAxis = idx, yAxis = idx, 
            borderColor = "#FFFFFF", borderWidth = 0.25,
            pointRange = 2, 
            name = paste(m, "Hist")
          ) %>%
          hc_add_series(
            data = pd$curve, type = "line", color = "#000000",
            xAxis = idx, yAxis = idx, 
            lineWidth = 1.5, marker = list(enabled = FALSE),
            name = paste(m, "Fit")
          )
      }
      return(hc)
    }
    
  } else {
    # case 2: single model plot
    m <- names(res)[[1]]
    pd <- get_plot_data_si(data, res[[1]])
    nm <- tolower(m)
    
    highchart() %>%
      hc_chart(style = list(fontFamily = "Jost"), backgroundColor = "#FFFFFF") %>%
      hc_title(text = paste(str_to_title(m), "Distribution"), style = list(fontSize="16px", fontWeight="bold")) %>%      
      hc_plotOptions(
        series = list(pointPlacement = "on"), 
        column = list(grouping = FALSE, pointPadding = 0, groupPadding = 0, borderWidth = 0.25)
      ) %>%
      hc_add_series(
        data = list_parse(pd$hist), type = "column", name = "Histogram",
        color = col_map[[nm]], borderColor = "#FFFFFF", borderWidth = 0.25,
        pointRange = 2
      ) %>%
      hc_add_series(
        data = pd$curve, type = "line", name = "Fit",
        color = "#000000", lineWidth = 1.5, marker = list(enabled = FALSE)
      ) %>%
      hc_xAxis(
        title = list(text = "Serial interval (days)", style = axis_style), 
        min = min_x_val, tickInterval = 2,
        lineColor = "#000000", lineWidth = 1, tickWidth = 1, tickColor = "#000000",
        labels = list(style = label_style),
        minPadding = 0, startOnTick = TRUE
      ) %>%
      hc_yAxis(
        title = list(text = "Density", style = axis_style),
        gridLineWidth = 0, lineWidth = 1, lineColor = "#000000", tickWidth = 1, tickColor = "#000000",
        labels = list(style = label_style),
        min = 0, minPadding = 0, startOnTick = TRUE
      ) %>%
      hc_exporting(enabled = TRUE, buttons = list(contextButton = list(menuItems = menu_items)), chartOptions = list(chart = list(backgroundColor = "#FFFFFF")))
  }
})
```

```{r}
renderDataTable({
  d <- si_checked()
  
  # ensure date columns are formatted as strings in yyyy-mm-dd
  d$date_of_exposure <- as.Date(d$date_of_exposure)
  d$date_of_onset <- as.Date(d$date_of_onset)
  d$source_date <- as.Date(d$source_date)
  
  # what the app made of the file comes first
  dataset <- dplyr::relocate(d, status, id, source_of_infection,
                             date_of_onset, source_date, serial_days)
  
  datatable(
    dataset,
    options = list(
```

```{r si-bayes-data-processing}

# data loading/processing
bayes_si_global <- reactive({
  req(input$file_bayes_si)
  tryCatch({
    df <- read.csv(input$file_bayes_si$datapath, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }, error = function(e) {
    validate(need(FALSE, "error reading file. please ensure it is a valid csv."))
  })
  names(df) <- tolower(names(df))
  names(df) <- gsub("\\.", "_", names(df))
  
  # validation start
  validate(
    need(all(c("id", "source_of_infection", "date_of_onsetmin", "date_of_onsetmax") %in% names(df)),
         "incorrect dataset: please upload serial bayesian data containing 'id', 'source of infection', 'date of onsetmin', and 'date of onsetmax'.")
  )
  # validation end
  
  # standardize sex
  if("sex" %in% names(df)) {
    df <- df %>% mutate(sex = case_when(
      grepl("^m", sex, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Male",
      grepl("^f", sex, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Female",
      TRUE ~ sex
    ))
  }
  
  # standardize age group
  col_age <- grep("age.*group", names(df), value = TRUE)[1]
  if(!is.na(col_age)) {
    df$age_clean <- df[[col_age]]
    df <- df %>% mutate(age_group = case_when(
      grepl("0-19|under 10|10s", age_clean, ignore.case=T) ~ '0 - 19',
      grepl("20s|20-29", age_clean, ignore.case=T) ~ '20 - 29',
      grepl("30s|30-39", age_clean, ignore.case=T) ~ '30 - 39',
      grepl("40s|40-49", age_clean, ignore.case=T) ~ '40 - 49',
      grepl("50s|50-59", age_clean, ignore.case=T) ~ '50 - 59',
      grepl("60s|70s|80s|60", age_clean, ignore.case=T) ~ '≥ 60',
      TRUE ~ 'Unknown'
    ))
  }
  
  df$id_clean <- trimws(gsub("#", "", df$id))
  df$source_clean <- trimws(gsub("#", "", df$source_of_infection))
  df$onset_min <- parse_date(df$date_of_onsetmin)
  df$onset_max <- parse_date(df$date_of_onsetmax)
  
  df
})

# filtering logic 
bayes_si_data <- reactive({
  req(bayes_si_global())
  
  # clean memory
  gc() 
  
  df <- bayes_si_global()
  
  df_infectors <- df 
  df_infectees <- df
  
  if (input$sex_bayes_si != "All" && "sex" %in% names(df)) {
    df_infectees <- df_infectees %>% filter(sex == input$sex_bayes_si)
  }
  if (input$age_bayes_si != "All" && "age_group" %in% names(df)) {
    df_infectees <- df_infectees %>% filter(age_group == input$age_bayes_si)
  }
  
  n_before_cleaning <- nrow(df_infectees)
  
  df_merged <- df_infectees %>%
    inner_join(df_infectors %>% dplyr::select(id_clean, onset_min, onset_max), 
               by = c("source_clean" = "id_clean"), 
               suffix = c("_infectee", "_infector"))
  
  df_final <- df_merged %>%
    filter(!is.na(onset_min_infectee), !is.na(onset_min_infector)) %>%
    mutate(
      tStartExposure = as.integer(onset_min_infector - as.Date("2019-12-31")),
      tEndExposure = as.integer(onset_max_infector - as.Date("2019-12-31")),
      tSymptomOnset = as.integer(onset_min_infectee - as.Date("2019-12-31")) + 
        as.integer(onset_max_infectee - onset_min_infectee)/2
    ) 
  
  # weibull, gamma and lognormal need a positive serial interval. rather than
  # dropping the pairs where the infectee fell ill before, or on the same day
  # as, the infector, the onsets are moved to the right by k days and the
  # fitted distribution is moved back when the results are shown. k covers the
  # whole exposure window, so every draw of tE stays below the onset. when no
  # pair needs it, k is 0 and nothing about the fit changes.
  si_shift <- 0
  if (input$bayes_model_select_si != "Normal" && nrow(df_final) > 0) {
    need <- max(df_final$tEndExposure - df_final$tSymptomOnset)
    if (need >= 0) {
      si_shift <- need + 1
      df_final$tSymptomOnset <- df_final$tSymptomOnset + si_shift
    }
  }
  df_final$si_shift <- si_shift
  
  n_final <- nrow(df_final)
  n_dropped <- n_before_cleaning - n_final
  
  if (n_dropped > 0) {
    showNotification(
      paste0("data loaded: ", n_final, " linked pairs found. (", n_dropped, " rows removed: unlinked or invalid dates)"),
      type = "warning", 
      duration = 5
    )
  } else {
    showNotification(
      paste0("data successfully loaded: ", n_final, " pairs ready."),
      type = "message", 
      duration = 3
    )
  }
  
  df_final
})

# every row of the selection, with the link the app resolved and a note of what
# became of it. a source of infection that is not itself a case in the file is
# reported here rather than quietly dropped by the join.
bayes_si_checked <- reactive({
  req(bayes_si_global())
  d <- bayes_si_global()
  if (input$sex_bayes_si != "All" && "sex" %in% names(d)) {
    d <- d %>% filter(sex == input$sex_bayes_si)
  }
  if (input$age_bayes_si != "All" && "age_group" %in% names(d)) {
    d <- d %>% filter(age_group == input$age_bayes_si)
  }
  
  full <- bayes_si_global()
  i <- match(d$source_clean, full$id_clean)
  d$onset_read          <- d$onset_min
  d$source_onset_read   <- full$onset_min[i]
  d$serial_days         <- as.numeric(d$onset_min - full$onset_min[i])
  known <- !is.na(d$source_clean) & nzchar(d$source_clean) & d$source_clean %in% full$id_clean
  d$status <- dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(d$onset_min)                             ~ "excluded: onset date could not be read",
    is.na(d$source_clean) | !nzchar(d$source_clean) ~ "excluded: no source of infection given",
    !known                                          ~ "excluded: the source of infection is not one of the case ids in this file",
    is.na(full$onset_min[i])                        ~ "excluded: the source case has no readable onset date",
    TRUE                                            ~ "used"
  )
  d
})

# modeling
bayes_si_fit <- eventReactive(input$run_bayes_si, {
  
  shinyjs::disable("run_bayes_si")
  
  on.exit({
    shinyjs::enable("run_bayes_si")
  })
  
  # cleanup
  gc()
  gc()
  
  req(bayes_si_data())
  df <- bayes_si_data()
  
  validate(
    need(nrow(df) >= 5, "insufficient data: you need at least 5 linked pairs.")
  )
  
  stan_data <- list(
    N = nrow(df),
    tStartExposure = df$tStartExposure,
    tEndExposure = df$tEndExposure,
    tSymptomOnset = df$tSymptomOnset
  )
  
  withProgress(message = 'running bayesian model...', detail = 'initializing...', value = 0, {
    
    mod <- get_compiled_stan_model(input$bayes_model_select_si)
    incProgress(0.1, detail = "sampling chains...")
    
    # run the sampling
    fit <- rstan::sampling(
      object = mod, 
      data = stan_data,
      chains = 4,
      cores = min(4, parallel::detectCores(), na.rm = TRUE),
      seed = STAN_SEED,
      iter = input$iter_count_si, 
      warmup = input$iter_count_si / 2,
      refresh = 0,
      # optimization: only save specific parameters to save ram
      pars = c("alphaInc", "sigmaInc"),
      control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95)
    )
    
    incProgress(0.8, detail = "extracting posteriors...")
    params <- rstan::extract(fit)
    
    # final cleanup after heavy processing
    gc()
    
    list(
      fit_obj = fit,
      iterations = input$iter_count_si,
      model_name = input$bayes_model_select_si,
      shift = if ("si_shift" %in% names(df)) df$si_shift[1] else 0,
      alpha = params$alphaInc,
      sigma = params$sigmaInc,
      alpha_summary = quantile(params$alphaInc, probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)),
      sigma_summary = quantile(params$sigmaInc, probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
    )
  })
})
```

### Model Statistics (Median & 95% CrI)

```{r si-bayes-model-stats}

renderDT({
  req(bayes_si_fit())
  res <- bayes_si_fit()
  
  # dynamic parameter labels
  if (res$model_name == "Lognormal") {
    p_names <- c("MeanLog (Alpha)", "SDLog (Sigma)")
    post_means <- exp(res$alpha + (res$sigma^2)/2)
  } else if (res$model_name == "Gamma") {
    p_names <- c("Shape (Alpha)", "Rate (Sigma)")
    post_means <- res$alpha / res$sigma
  } else if (res$model_name == "Normal") {
    p_names <- c("Mean (Alpha)", "SD (Sigma)")
    post_means <- res$alpha # mean is just alpha for normal
  } else {
    p_names <- c("Shape (Alpha)", "Scale (Sigma)")
    post_means <- res$sigma * gamma(1 + 1/res$alpha)
  }
  
  df_stats <- data.frame(
    Parameter = p_names,
    `Median` = round(c(res$alpha_summary[2], res$sigma_summary[2]), 3),
    `Lower_95_CrI` = round(c(res$alpha_summary[1], res$sigma_summary[1]), 3),
    `Upper_95_CrI` = round(c(res$alpha_summary[3], res$sigma_summary[3]), 3)
  )
  
  # the model was fitted to serial intervals moved to the right by res$shift,
  # so the mean is moved back before it is shown
  si_shift <- if (!is.null(res$shift)) res$shift else 0
  mean_summ <- quantile(post_means - si_shift, probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
  
  df_mean <- data.frame(
    Parameter = "Mean Serial Interval",
    `Median` = round(mean_summ[2], 3),
    `Lower_95_CrI` = round(mean_summ[1], 3),
    `Upper_95_CrI` = round(mean_summ[3], 3)
  )
  
  final_df <- rbind(df_stats, df_mean)
  
  # make the shift visible: the two parameters above describe the shifted
  # distribution, the mean has been moved back on to the observed scale
  if (si_shift > 0) {
    final_df <- rbind(final_df, data.frame(
      Parameter = "Shift applied (days)",
      Median = si_shift, Lower_95_CrI = NA, Upper_95_CrI = NA
    ))
  }
  
  fname <- paste0("Serial_Interval_Bayesian_Stats_", Sys.Date())
  
  datatable(
    final_df, 
    rownames = FALSE, 
    extensions = 'Buttons',
    options = list(
      dom = 'Brt',
      buttons = list(
        list(extend = "csv", filename = fname),
        list(extend = "excel", filename = fname),
        list(extend = "pdf", filename = fname)
      ),
      columnDefs = list(list(className = 'dt-center', targets = "_all"))
    )
  ) %>%
    formatStyle(columns = "Parameter", fontWeight = "bold")
})
```

### Posterior Distribution (Median Fit)

```{r si-bayes-posterior-dist}

renderHighchart({
  req(bayes_si_fit())
  res <- bayes_si_fit()
  
  alpha_est <- median(res$alpha)
  sigma_est <- median(res$sigma)
  si_shift  <- if (!is.null(res$shift)) res$shift else 0
  
  # dynamic x-axis range logic
  if (res$model_name == "Normal") {
    # calculate lower bound to capture negative tail (99.9% coverage)
    lower_bound <- qnorm(0.001, mean = alpha_est, sd = sigma_est)
    # cap upper bound at 30 for comparability
    upper_bound <- 30
    x_vals <- seq(lower_bound, upper_bound, length.out = 300)
    x_min_limit <- NULL # let chart auto-scale to show negatives
  } else {
    # strictly positive models are fitted on the shifted scale, so the density
    # is calculated there and drawn back on the observed scale below
    x_vals <- seq(0, 30 + si_shift, length.out = 300)
    x_min_limit <- if (si_shift > 0) NULL else 0
  }
  
  # dynamic density calculation
  if (res$model_name == "Gamma") {
    y_vals <- dgamma(x_vals, shape = alpha_est, rate = sigma_est)
  } else if (res$model_name == "Lognormal") {
    y_vals <- dlnorm(x_vals, meanlog = alpha_est, sdlog = sigma_est)
  } else if (res$model_name == "Normal") {
    y_vals <- dnorm(x_vals, mean = alpha_est, sd = sigma_est)
  } else {
    y_vals <- dweibull(x_vals, shape = alpha_est, scale = sigma_est)
  }
  
  model_label <- tools::toTitleCase(res$model_name)
  menu_items <- list("viewFullscreen", "separator", "downloadPNG", "downloadPDF", "downloadSVG")
  axis_style <- list(color = "#000000", fontSize = "14px", fontWeight = "bold", fontFamily = "Jost")
  
  highchart() %>%
    hc_chart(
      style = list(fontFamily = "Jost"), 
      backgroundColor = "#FFFFFF"
    ) %>%
    
    hc_title(
      text = paste0("Posterior Predictive Distribution (", model_label, ")"),
      style = list(fontSize = "18px", fontWeight = "bold", fontFamily = "Jost", color = "#000000")
    ) %>%
    
    hc_subtitle(
      text = paste0("Based on ", res$iterations, " MCMC iterations"),
      style = list(fontSize = "14px", fontFamily = "Jost", color = "#666666")
    ) %>%
    
    hc_exporting(
      enabled = TRUE, 
      filename = paste0("Serial_Interval_Posterior_Distribution_", Sys.Date()),
      buttons = list(contextButton = list(menuItems = menu_items))
    ) %>%
    
    hc_add_series(
      data = data.frame(x = x_vals - si_shift, y = y_vals), 
      type = "area", 
      name = "Posterior Density", 
      color = "rgba(255, 140, 0, 0.5)",
      lineWidth = 2
    ) %>%
    
    hc_xAxis(
      title = list(text = "Serial Interval (Days)", style = axis_style), 
      labels = list(style = axis_style),
      min = x_min_limit,
      minPadding = 0,
      startOnTick = TRUE,
      lineColor = "#000000", 
      lineWidth = 1, 
      tickColor = "#000000"
    ) %>%
    
    hc_yAxis(
      title = list(text = "Density", style = axis_style), 
      labels = list(style = axis_style),
      min = 0, 
      minPadding = 0, 
      startOnTick = TRUE,
      gridLineWidth = 0, 
      lineColor = "#000000", 
      lineWidth = 1, 
      tickColor = "#000000"
    ) %>%
    
    hc_tooltip(valueDecimals = 4, style = list(fontFamily = "Jost"))
})

```
